title: Adaptive transport presets and connection hygiene for SDKs (Python/TS/Go)
creator: Ava Chen
description: Scope: Create cross-SDK (Python, TypeScript, Go) transport presets and adaptive heuristics for request timeouts, connection pooling/keep-alive, and general connection hygiene. Deliverables: 1) A small set of documented presets (low_latency, high_throughput, conservative) that map to unified config keys across SDKs; 2) Adaptive timeout heuristics that adjust request/idle timeouts based on observed tail latency and error rates; 3) Connection pool sizing guidance and default values tuned per language runtime and HTTP stack (http1/http2/gRPC); 4) Streaming ergonomics guidance (reconnect/backoff, cancelation ergonomics, example patterns for long-lived streams); 5) Telemetry and e2e tests to validate regressions. Motivation: Customers frequently hit tail latency or resource exhaustion when adopting streaming or bursty workloads. SDKs currently ship language-defaults that either cause too many short-lived connections or hold connections forever, increasing costs and TLS handshake overhead. This ticket standardizes a pragmatic set of defaults and a lightweight adaptive layer so teams can get predictable behavior without deep ops tuning.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Created by Ava: initial problem statement and scope. Noted repeated support tickets where customers saw elevated TLS handshakes and socket exhaustion on low-traffic hosts.

2026-03-02 - Miguel: Proposed config model: transport.protocol, transport.pool.max_connections, transport.pool.keepalive_seconds, transport.pool.idle_timeout_seconds, transport.timeout.connect_ms, transport.timeout.request_ms, transport.timeout.stream_inactivity_ms. Will implement shims per SDK to map to language idioms.
2026-03-03 - PM review (Sofia Patel): prioritize low_latency preset for PLG onboarding; conservative preset for enterprise (saves connections). Add a recommended preset for dedicated deployments.

2026-03-04 - Design (Elliot Wong): Suggested UX for Console docs and quickstart: show a preset selector and an inline snippet for Python/TS/Go. Approved the unified keys but asked for examples showing how to override per-route.

2026-03-05 - Engineering notes: running microbenchmarks. Observed on Linux kernel 5.4 HTTP/2 GO client has a spike in handshake time when creating >150 connections concurrently. Added a safety cap + connection ramp strategy in the high_throughput preset.

2026-03-06 - Decision: Use exponential backoff with jitter for stream reconnects; provide configurable max-retries and idempotency-aware default (0 for non-idempotent streaming writes). Document cancellation semantics in each SDK's async/await/callback models.

2026-03-08 - PRs opened: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/412, github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/519, github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/274. These include preset wiring and telemetry hooks (connection_age_seconds, pool_active, pool_idle, request_connect_latency_ms, tls_handshake_ms).

2026-03-09 - QA: Added e2e test harness that spins up a local HTTP/2 gateway and runs bursty request patterns and long-lived streams. Found an edge case where TypeScript's fetch polyfill closed sockets aggressively on Node <18; added runtime detection and fallback.

2026-03-10 - Blocker identified by Security: need to validate keepalive settings do not interfere with corporate proxy behavior for customers behind strict proxies. Security asked for a review before GA. Marking ticket for security review gate.
Next steps: finish PR feedback, add console docs snippets, complete security review, run canary in dedicated infra, and schedule SDK minor releases with migration notes.
